newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE to monitor Chechnya election.
newsitem.headline: OSCE to monitor Chechnya election.

text.p: Europe's security body will send observers to monitor elections in the breakaway region of Chechnya due on January 27, an OSCE official told Reuters on Thursday.
"The OSCE (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe) will send election monitors to Chechnya," an OSCE spokeswoman in Vienna said.
Tim Guldimann, who heads the OSCE mission in Chechnya, was due to address the security body's permanent council on Thursday ahead of a final decision.
"We expect the OSCE states today will support this election-monitoring effort," the spokeswoman said.

Guldimann said last week that a spate of recent violence in Chechnya, including the shooting of a group of Russians and the murder of six foreign Red Cross workers, made him fear further assassinations.
But preparations were underway for at least 50 observers to monitor the elections after 21 months of war, providing the republic could guarantee their safety, he said.
The elections are scheduled for January 27, and are backed by Russian authorities, despite unresolved differences over the issue of the republic's independence.

Under a deal struck in August, Moscow and the rebels agreed to postpone the issue of Chechnya's political status for five years in return for a withdrawal of Russian troops from the region. Russia announced on January 5 it had pulled its last Interior Ministry troops from the province.

The separatists are keen to have foreign observers present during voting to add legitimacy to the elections, which they see as a first step towards an independence recognised beyond Chechen frontiers.
